title: Choose the visual world for PDF Forms
question: The roll assigned The Filing Room — a courthouse-docket system where templates are case files, links are docket entries, and submissions are stamped filings. Keep it, take an alternate, or re-roll.

options.label: The Filing Room
options.thesis: Every template is a case file, every link a docket entry, every submission a stamped filing — never a card in a dashboard.
options.viewport: A docket register: tab-indexed rail on the left, case-file cards stamped with a docket number and a red FILED/PENDING mark, kraft dividers between sections.
options.risk: Reads bureaucratic instead of confident if the stamp motif spreads past status markers into decoration.

raised.raise: Status reads as an exact measured fact — "Filed 08/17 2:14 PM" — never a vague relative label.
Hierarchy comes from weight and scale on a strict baseline grid, not boxes or card shadows.
Opening a case file or link detail slides and hinges open like pulling a folder from the rail, not a flat modal fade.

options.label: The Ledger
options.thesis: The whole product as one ruled ledger — templates, links, and submissions are rows in a worksheet, not cards in a grid.
options.viewport: A single continuous worksheet: ruled column headers, monospaced figures, a totals rule closing each section.
options.risk: Familiar territory — tabular, spreadsheet-adjacent UI is common in fintech/accounting SaaS already, so it risks reading expected rather than distinct.

options.label: The Seasonal Folio
options.lineage: botanical folio plates, fixed-scale seasonal sequence
options.thesis: Every submission plate aligns on the same scale and baseline, so an empty template and a filled one read as two states of one plant.
options.viewport: Fixed-scale plates in a row — template, in-progress, filed — sharing one baseline and caption strip.
options.case: Fuses cleanly on clarity: the fixed-scale comparative-plate device makes template-vs-filled states directly legible. Loses narrowly on audience identification — legal/accounting clients don't live in botanical-illustration culture the way they live in filing culture.
options.risk: The plate palette drifts toward the warm cream-and-sepia default this brief must avoid unless pushed cooler and inkier than a literal botanical plate.

options.label: Sneaker Archive Wall
options.lineage: stacked sneaker-box archive, silhouette end labels
options.case: Fuses poorly: legal and accounting clients hold no relationship to collector/streetwear culture, and the mapping (template = box) doesn't clarify the mechanism.
options.kept: Tactile pull-open retrieval motion — raised into the assigned direction.

options.label: Dawn Cyclorama
options.case: Fuses poorly: theatrical lighting has no bearing on a legal client's scene, and the atmospheric night-to-day metaphor clarifies status less than a literal stamp does.
options.kept: Smooth continuous state transitions over abrupt swaps — noted, not raised: a status the client must trust reads clearer as a literal stamp change than a mood shift.

options.label: Generative Parametric Identity
options.case: Fuses poorly: a mark and palette that visibly mutate undermine trust for a client entering real personal and financial information — the opposite of what this surface needs to prove.
options.kept: One seed governing every token — folded in as ordinary design-system discipline, not a raise; the product needs stability, not live mutation.

options.label: Signal Bench Oscilloscope
options.lineage: CRT oscilloscope, phosphor trace on graticule
options.case: Fuses poorly: an electronics-lab instrument reads as a dev tool, not a law office, undermining the trust a legal client needs on first look.
options.kept: Exact, measured state readouts — raised into the assigned direction.

options.label: Interactive Type Specimen
options.case: Fuses poorly: a type-foundry demo has no functional mapping to document collection, and foundry/type-nerd culture isn't the legal client's world.
options.kept: Scale/weight-driven hierarchy on a strict grid — raised into the assigned direction.

canonCard.label: The Document Portal Standard
canonCard.thesis: Clean white cards, blue accent, rounded corners — instantly familiar, instantly forgettable.
canonCard.viewport: Sidebar nav, card grid of templates, pill badges for status — the arrangement every document SaaS ships.
canonCard.risk: Indistinguishable from DocuSign, HelloSign, or any other forms tool, by design.
